notes.text: You wrote to Campus France New Delhi this morning and copied Fitria, so the transfer now waits on Delhi. Your email says you fly to India on 4 November and will apply through New Delhi VFS, so Friday's TLS date here is dead. - Give it a date you expect to use, or clear it until Delhi answers.

notes.text: Chitra wrote this morning asking whether you are renewing or cancelling the KITAS, and the revised quotation for cancellation, NPWP and BPJS is still unanswered. She notes renewal normally starts a month before the 8 November expiry, so that window has closed. - Tell her you are cancelling, since you leave on the 4th.

notes.itemTitle: Decide on Business Foundations and register
notes.title: Last call on Business Foundations
notes.text: INSEAD sent its final reminder this morning: registration and the 1,530 euro payment both close on 30 October, and the module runs 16 to 20 November online. Your task still waits on the SBI sanction, which is dated 10 November. - Worth deciding this week, since the loan will not have landed either way.

notes.title: LMS opens tomorrow
notes.text: INSEAD says the LMS goes live by end of day on 26 October, reached from a new My Courses tab on MyINSEAD. Three tiles to start: Programme Management, PLDP with its mandatory P0 assignments, and CDC with the career webinar sign-ups. - Your task is dated the same day, so give it the evening or move it.

notes.text: INSEAD is running an Ask Me Anything on the French visa tomorrow, 12:00 Paris for 45 minutes, open to anyone who has not applied yet. Your route through Delhi is unusual enough to be worth asking about live. - The registration link is in Bi Hui Ko's email this morning.

notes.text: There is an online Meet Your Class session on 29 October, 16:00 Paris. The in-person admit events are Madrid, Dubai, Toronto and Milan, so none of them is reachable from where you are. - The online one is the only one you can make.

kb.label: IAA Alumni Meet & Greet
kb.body: The INSEAD Alumni Association's own introduction to the network: who they are, what the regional chapters do, and how alumni actually get used during and after the MBA. Optional in INSEAD's own rating, and the one P0 session that is about the twenty years after the degree rather than the year of it.

kb.label: PLDP intro webinar
kb.body: On Zoom. Walks through the Personal Leadership Development Programme: what the P0 assignments ask for, how individual and group coaching fit together across the year, and what your coach does with what you write. INSEAD marks this MUST DO, and it is the session that makes the assignment window make sense rather than feel like homework.

kb.label: AMA on student platforms
kb.body: An open question session on the tools you are about to live in: the LMS, CareerGlobe, and the rest of the stack. Optional, and worth it only if something in the platforms is already confusing you by then.

kb.label: INSEAD CV & Cover Letter webinar
kb.body: 13:00 Paris / 20:00 Singapore. What belongs in the INSEAD CV format and what gets cut, how recruiters read it, and where the CV work sits in the year: a first draft through VMock before a human sees it, then review with your coach, and the CV Book after that. Must-do for career switchers.

kb.label: Academics overview webinar
kb.body: On Zoom, with the MBA Programme Management Director and current students. The curriculum end to end, how the core and electives fit, exemptions, and what people wish they had done before arriving. Highly recommended rather than required, and the one place to ask a second-hand question about workload.

kb.label: Your Summer Experience & Prep for Arrival
kb.body: The three honest ways to spend the eight-week break after P3: a short-term summer project with a company, a startup tour, or deliberate time off to prepare for full-time recruitment. Also covers arrival logistics. This is the session that decides what you spend P2 recruiting for.

kb.label: Business Foundations: register by 30 October
kb.body: The course itself runs one week online, 16-20 November: an intensive introduction to Financial Accounting, Finance and Quantitative Methods aimed at people arriving without a quant background. Optional, registered through MyINSEAD, and the decision has to be made three weeks before it runs.

kb.label: CareerLeader and Career Anchors, before the first coaching session
kb.body: Two profiling questionnaires plus the workbook questions that go with them. They are the entire raw material for the first coaching conversation, so the session is only as good as what you put in: arriving without them turns a 45-minute slot into an introduction you could have had by email. The CDC's mail of 12 October carries the mechanism: register at careerleader.com as a new user with your INSEAD address and the registration key that mail holds — the key is deliberately not recorded here, because this repository is public — then complete the profile and the three assessments and keep the report for the session. Career Anchors is an Excel workbook downloaded from INSEAD's own site. Thirty minutes and twenty, so both fit in one evening. Coaching slots open in early November.

kb.label: PLDP assignments window
kb.body: Delivered online through the LMS across roughly seven weeks. Your coach reads these before meeting you, so they are what shapes the coaching you get rather than a box to tick. INSEAD marks them MUST DO, and the window deliberately spans the December break because they are not a single sitting.

kb.label: Launch Week career pre-work appears on the LMS
kb.body: Posted in early December, to be completed before Launch Week rather than during it. Launch Week is dense enough that anything left undone gets done badly or not at all, and the career workshop assumes the pre-work is behind you.

kb.label: P0, the pre-programme period
kb.body: Where the board is right now: the twelve weeks between the LMS going live and Launch Week. Three strands run through it at once -- Academics, Careers and Student Life -- and almost everything in the Webinars and Deadlines blocks sits inside this stretch. It ends the day Launch Week begins.

kb.label: Launch Week
kb.body: Fontainebleau, eleven days. The P1 core exemption exams sit inside it along with orientation, the career workshop and the first run of sessions that set up P1. The pre-work that goes with it lands on the LMS in early December.

kb.label: Period dates, P1 to P5
kb.body: Five eight-week periods across eleven months, with a long summer gap in the middle. INSEAD publishes these as provisional and says they can still move, so treat anything booked around the edges as provisional too.

kb.label: Breaks
kb.body: Three short ones and the long summer. The short breaks are not empty: career treks and club treks run in them, which is most of what people mean when they say the MBA has no holidays. The 1 July to 22 August gap is the one the summer project fits inside.

kb.label: Campus exchange bidding happens during P1
kb.body: Campus is Fontainebleau or Singapore for P1 and P2; exchange opens from P3 onwards, and the bidding for it runs inside P1 while you are still finding your feet. The rules change year to year, so the P1 briefing is the authority rather than anything written now.

kb.label: Graduation, Singapore
kb.body: Singapore campus, with the grad trip after it. Twenty-three months from the deposit to the gown.

kb.label: LMS
kb.body: Live from 26 October. Every piece of academic content runs through it, a chunk of the CDC curriculum as well, and club registration too. The PLDP assignments are delivered here.

kb.label: CareerGlobe
kb.body: Live from 27 October. The CDC platform: appointments, jobs, events. The profile has to be set up before you can book the first coaching appointment, which makes it the gate on everything else CDC.

kb.label: VMock
kb.body: Part 1 of the INSEAD CV process. It scores a draft against the format and tells you what to fix, so the version a human finally reads is not the first one you wrote.

kb.label: The INSEAD CV format
kb.body: One format, used as a networking and marketing document rather than a record of employment, and the basis for the INSEAD CV Book that goes to recruiters. The process runs on through P1, so the first version is not the last.

kb.label: Two teams behind you: a Career Coach and Employer Engagement
kb.body: That is the whole of CDC's structure, and it is worth knowing which one to ask. The coach is your primary contact for strategy, materials and accountability. Employer Engagement are the sector specialists who know what a given industry is actually hiring for this year.

kb.label: Coaching sessions are 45 minutes and you set the agenda
kb.body: Short enough to fit before class, which is deliberate. You bring the update and the question and agree the next steps; the coach pressure-tests the plan rather than making it. A session you arrive at without having done the last set of next steps is a session spent recapping.

kb.label: Your coach is allocated on P1 location and never changes
kb.body: Deliberately coach-agnostic: they are allocated by where you start, follow you the whole MBA including exchange, and there are no coach changes. So the relationship is worth investing in early rather than shopping around.

kb.label: First coaching session, from November
kb.body: Covers how the partnership works, what CareerLeader and Career Anchors said about you, and the three stages of the career journey. CareerGlobe has to be set up before you can book it.

kb.label: The career journey is three stages
kb.body: Self Awareness: strengths, interests, values, and what you actually bring. Market Exploration: industry knowledge built through networking, narrowed to two or three target plans rather than one bet or ten. Execution: a value proposition you can say out loud, and recruiting to each sector's real timetable, which differs by months.

kb.label: Career switcher status decides how much of CDC is must-do
kb.body: Most CDC items are marked must-do for people switching Location, Sector or Function, and only highly recommended for everyone else. Which of the three you are switching is therefore the single input that sets your CDC workload, and it is worth writing down early.

kb.label: Employer Engagement are Sector Advisors
kb.body: Subject-matter experts who split their time between advising students and talking to companies, which is what makes their market read current. They give market intelligence, name who to connect with, sharpen a pitch for a specific sector, and help with offer negotiation.

kb.label: Careers Across Geographies & Sectors workshop
kb.body: February 2027, for Fontainebleau and Singapore. CDC asks 27Ds not to book Sector Advisor appointments until after it, because most of the sector information is delivered there and a one-to-one before it just repeats the workshop. The one exception is roles with early internship application deadlines.

kb.label: Company events, treks and the Industry Expert Series
kb.body: Pre-MBA company event invitations arrive through the Sunday newsletters, which is the practical reason to read them. During the year there are treks, networking forums, the Tech Symposium and the Industry Expert Series.

kb.label: CDC's own key takeaways
kb.body: Networking is what works: alumni first, then people in the target industry, then classmates. Pick a few priorities rather than defaulting to consulting because it recruits loudest. Take a leadership role in a club. A radical career changer should start before the programme, not in P1. If you are targeting one country with no experience there, explore widely early and aim at roles where local competition is thinner. And only apply where you genuinely fit, because the interview exposes the rest.

kb.label: PLDP runs the whole year, not just P0
kb.body: The Personal Leadership Development Programme: individual and group coaching that starts with the P0 assignments and continues across the periods. It is the leadership counterpart to CDC's career coaching, and it is the one INSEAD flags as high-importance alongside CDC.

kb.label: Internship recruiting runs through P2
kb.body: March to May 2027. Some internships start as early as June, before P3 finishes. Roles with early application deadlines are the one reason to approach Employer Engagement before the February workshop.

kb.label: The summer project itself: optional, 8 weeks
kb.body: A Short-Term Summer Project in the break after P3. The alternatives INSEAD names are a startup tour or deliberate time off to prepare for full-time recruitment, and it does not treat the internship as obligatory for this cohort. Gavin's own plan is to start looking from the day the course starts rather than waiting for P2.

kb.label: Six P1 core courses
kb.body: Financial Accounting, Financial Markets & Valuation, Organisational Behaviour I, Prices & Markets, Uncertainty Data & Judgment, and Introduction to Strategy. Three of the six are quantitative, which is what Business Foundations exists for.

kb.label: P1 pre-readings
kb.body: For Financial Accounting and Prices & Markets specifically, with book recommendations on the MBA Journey pages. Highly recommended rather than required, which in practice means the people who do them have an easier first three weeks.

kb.label: Core exemption exams
kb.body: P1 core exemptions are examined during Launch Week; P2 and P3 exemptions are taken during P1. Passing one frees the slot for an elective, so an exemption is worth a course you would rather take than a week of revision saved.

kb.label: Club introduction and registration
kb.body: Runs through the LMS from 26 October. Club leadership elections and the handover to the 27D cohort come in P1 and P2, so the clubs you join now are the ones you can take a leadership role in later, which CDC names as one of its key takeaways.

kb.label: 27D Student Council and Student Rep elections
kb.body: January 2027. Team diversity is a stated requirement for the slates, so the teams form before the election rather than after it.

kb.label: Programme questions
kb.body: degree.programmes@insead.edu for anything about the programme itself: dates, registration, admin, documents.

kb.label: Career questions
kb.body: careerdevelopmentcentre@insead.edu for CDC: coaching, CareerGlobe, Employer Engagement, anything career.

kb.label: Career Coach
kb.body: Your primary contact all year. Career strategy, target and transferable skills, networking approach, CV and cover letter review, elevator pitch, mock interviews, choosing between offers, and holding you accountable.

kb.label: MBA-Exchange.com
kb.body: The CDC's third-party global careers platform, premium access through INSEAD's partnership: vetted postings, industry and country reports, employer profiles with Talent Radar visibility, and Talent Talks with recruiters. The welcome mail arrived on 5 October with a login of your INSEAD address and a password in plain text, so change that password on first login — the password itself is deliberately not recorded here, because this repository is public. Bilal Ojjeh, their founder, offers himself as the direct contact.

kb.label: Aced, formerly Exponent
kb.body: Technical interview preparation, free through an INSEAD invitation that landed on 5 October: courses in software engineering, SQL and data analytics and system design, mock technical interviews, a question bank of recently asked questions, and company-by-company hiring guides. Sign up at aced.io with the INSEAD address the invitation was sent to. It is the one career platform aimed at technical interviews rather than the consulting-and-finance case track that CaseCoach covers.

kb.label: CaseCoach
kb.body: Case interview preparation, free on the INSEAD subscription, which you registered for on 5 October. Their own course opens with what to expect from a case interview and is reading rather than a task; the founder, Enguerran Loos, is a former consultant and headhunter for the top three firms. It is the consulting-and-finance counterpart to Aced's technical track, and the one to work through if consulting stays on your list.

kb.label: Why the pre-MBA window had already closed
kb.body: McKinsey's Make Your Mark, BCG Unlock and Bain's ExperienceBain are all aimed at people who have been admitted and have not started yet, and they run over the northern summer: registration falls roughly May to July, the programme itself August to December. That is built around an autumn intake. The January 2027 intake's equivalent window had passed before the admission letter arrived, which is why Make Your Mark was never a thing that could have been applied to from here. Nothing was missed through not looking; the calendar simply does not line up. What replaces it is the on-campus cycle, which starts in P1.

kb.label: McKinsey Make Your Mark
kb.body: A pre-MBA mentorship programme for incoming MBA students at a named set of schools, INSEAD among them: one-to-one mentoring with a McKinsey consultant, recruiting workshops, networking and interview coaching, running from late August to the end of December. Applications have closed in July in recent cycles. It is a mentorship and a foot in the door rather than an offer, and the thing it actually buys is knowing how the firm recruits before everyone else does.

kb.label: BCG Unlock
kb.body: BCG's pre-MBA virtual event series: sessions with BCG leaders and consultants on what consulting work is, plus skill-building and networking, over the summer before the programme starts. Registration has been encouraged by mid-May and then reviewed on a rolling basis after that. Virtual, so geography is not the constraint - the admission timing is.

kb.label: ExperienceBain
kb.body: Bain's virtual pre-MBA programme for incoming first-years at eligible schools: interactive sessions with Bain teams around the world across the summer, flexible rather than a fixed week. Recent cycles have closed applications in early May. Same shape and the same timing problem as the other two.

kb.label: Amazon Pathways (MBA Operations LDP)
kb.body: Amazon's three-year operations leadership development programme, open to people enrolled in an MBA or within 24 months of graduating, with cohorts tied to a start year rather than a single deadline. There is no closing date at all: applications are read on a rolling basis and the posting comes down when they have enough people, which makes early the whole strategy. It is the closest fit on the Big Tech list to five years of SaaS presales and operations - a management track rather than a functional hire.

kb.label: How the Big Tech and consumer cycles are timed
kb.body: Both run on graduation year, not on intake. The 2027 postings at Amazon, J&J and their peers say "graduating between August 2026 and August 2027", which a December 2027 graduation sits outside - so the cycle that matters is the one that opens in autumn 2027, and anything open now is worth applying to only where the eligibility text actually admits it. The practical consequence: the autumn 2027 window is the one to be ready for, and the preparation for it (CV, CareerGlobe, the CDC coach) is already on the board.

kb.label: What the Sunday brief watches
kb.body: Every Sunday the weekly report carries a NEWS section: pre-MBA and in-programme opportunities researched against the three target groups - Big Tech LDP and management-track roles, MBB consulting, and consumer LDPs. Anything worth doing becomes a task titled [NEWS], drawn in magenta, with Accept and Reject on its card. A week with nothing says so rather than padding. This group is where the findings that are facts rather than tasks collect.

kb.label: The French APS is France-only, and it is the thing that removes sponsorship
kb.body: Graduating at Fontainebleau makes him a French master's graduate, which entitles him to the APS (autorisation provisoire de sejour, also called the RECE) -- a residence permit that lets him work in France without an employer sponsoring anything. That is the answer to the barrier he hit when job-hunting: outside France an employer has to sponsor from scratch, in France it only has to convert a permit he already holds. The permit is national, so it carries no right to work in Germany, Spain or the Netherlands, and the usual quoted length is 12 months with sources disagreeing about a longer window for Indian nationals. Its real value is as a bridge: a year of legal French employment is what makes the next two routes available.

kb.label: How a French job becomes a job anywhere in the EU
kb.body: Two mechanisms, both on a clock that only starts once he is employed. The EU Blue Card is issued for a graduate-level job above a salary threshold, and after roughly twelve months in the first country it allows a move to another EU state on a simplified application rather than a fresh sponsorship. EU long-term residence arrives at five years of legal residence and carries broad mobility with it. So the sequence that actually works is France first on the APS, convert to a Blue Card, then move -- not applying cold into the Netherlands or Spain from outside.

kb.label: Where to aim: France, the Netherlands, Ireland -- and why not Switzerland
kb.body: France is the base because the APS makes it the one country with no permission problem. The Netherlands is the strongest second: English-language workplaces are normal, Amsterdam carries real tech and consumer headquarters, and quality of life is high. Ireland is the third, with Dublin holding the European seats of Google, Meta, Microsoft and Stripe and a Critical Skills Employment Permit that is comparatively straightforward. Switzerland is ruled out despite the salaries -- non-EU hires face a labour market test and a national quota, which is exactly the barrier he is trying to avoid. Spain is the leisure-weighted alternative and became more plausible once he said he already speaks basic Spanish and can reach decent proficiency by graduation; it is thinner on Big Tech but Barcelona and Madrid are real markets. Belgium is the underrated one: the lowest salary bar of the group. Singapore stays a maybe on the Employment Pass and COMPASS framework. The structural point behind all of it: pick the employer first and the country follows, because a multinational moves people between its own offices far more easily than a new employer sponsors a stranger.

kb.label: A summer internship abroad needs its own permission, and it is not the student visa
kb.body: His French student residence permit covers work in France and nothing outside it, so each of the internship markets has its own route. Ireland uses the Atypical Working Scheme, which must be applied for from outside Ireland and wants at least twelve weeks' notice -- that lead time is the one that bites, since the applications close in November for a July start. Luxembourg requires a trainee authorisation arranged by the host company. The UK route is Temporary Work -- Government Authorised Exchange, again employer-led. The United States is possible rather than closed: the J-1 Intern category explicitly covers students enrolled at a university outside the US, but a State Department designated sponsor has to issue the DS-2019, so it depends entirely on whether the employer already runs that programme. The practical rule is to ask the recruiter which route they use before assuming an offer is workable.

kb.label: The Dutch orientation year probably does not apply to an INSEAD degree
kb.body: The zoekjaar is the Netherlands' post-study search year, and it is open either to graduates of a Dutch institution or to graduates of a university in the global top 200 of QS, Times Higher Education or ARWU. INSEAD is a business school and does not appear in those general university rankings, so the second door is likely shut -- worth confirming with Nuffic before counting on it. The consequence is that the Dutch route runs through an employer and a Blue Card rather than through a job-search permit, which makes the timing different: the offer has to come first.

kb.label: The 27D job report is the CDC's live list of what is open now
kb.body: A spreadsheet circulated with the newsletter, listing roles open to the 27D cohort with company, title, location, type and deadline. It mixes full-time graduate roles with summer internships and the type column is not always right -- a Google row tagged full-time is titled MBA intern. It is the source the five application tasks on the board came from, and it is reissued, so it is worth re-reading each time rather than treating the current shortlist as final. Deadlines on it run close: four of the five chosen roles close on 8 November.

news.body:
## Tomorrow
- Plan Locus exit, due 7 Oct, and the only Critical thing with a date this week.
There is no resignation date, no notice period and no last working day on the board. What last working day are you aiming for, and do you owe notice? The January move hangs off that one date.

## Not yours right now
- Campus France, corrected preconsular file sent yesterday afternoon.
Nothing to do but wait. What it gates: EEF validation reads 21 Oct and the VFS appointment is 10 Nov, so there is about three weeks of slack behind it. If validation slips past the 21st, that slack is gone.
- SBI sanction letter, due 24 Oct.
The PoA was executed at Hindon on 3 Oct, so the bank should have everything. Is anything still outstanding from your side, or is it purely theirs now?

## Worth an hour this week
- VMock and CaseCoach both went live yesterday, good.
The CDC mail that came with them wants CareerLeader and Career Anchors done before your first coaching session, which is why booking the coach still reads as blocked. They are due 31 Oct and take an hour or two. Start with CareerLeader: it is the longer one and it feeds the report the CDC asks for.

## The passport is the decision now
- TLS keeps your passport from the day you submit, now dated 23 October, for two to three weeks.
Three things want it in that window: the exit permit for your KITAS, your flight out of Jakarta, and the visa itself. The ways out are different enough that choosing is the work -- submit before you leave and ask whether someone else can collect, apply from India after you land, or move your departure. Tell me which and I will set every date after it accordingly.
- The 16 October interview still waits on a courier.
Your originals reach you early next week, and Fitria postpones the interview if they are not in your hand on the day. Tracking on that parcel is what would let you confirm the slot rather than hope.

## Nothing here waits on anyone
- Create your France-Visas and TLS Contact accounts.
Fitria asked for both and neither needs the interview done first, so this is the one piece of the visa you can finish today.
- Upload your CV to VMock, 18 October.
The next date on the board that is nobody's but yours, and it is a short job.

## Wednesday's interview is the whole visa now
- Campus France put you at 10:00 on Wednesday 14 October, two days earlier than the board had it.
Fitria gave you the earliest slot you asked for, and the originals still have to be in your hand on the day, so the courier is the only thing standing between you and it. A tracking number today is what turns Wednesday from a hope into a plan.
- Submitting at TLS two working days after the interview, rather than on the 23rd, is what saves your flight.
Fitria put submission about two working days after the interview and a decision about fifteen days after that. From 16 October that lands at the end of the month; from the 23rd it lands on 7 November, the day you leave Jakarta. Creating your France-Visas and TLS Contact accounts this weekend is what lets you book the slot the moment the interview ends.

## The loan has less slack than it looks
- The SBI sanction is dated 24 October and the 5 November instalment sits behind it.
Your branch has not come back since you told them on 6 October that the charges confirmation went on the 3rd. Monday is a working day there, and a call to the branch will move this where another email has not.

## What moved
- You cleared the Campus France file and two of the career platforms.
The EEF was validated and the fee paid on 6 October, the extra documents went on the 5th, and VMock access and Case Coach were both closed the same day. Five tasks closed in the week, all of them yours rather than anyone else's.
- The visa turned out to be three weeks earlier than the board thought.
Campus France refused the interview exemption on Thursday, which revived a task you had deleted, and in the same conversation Fitria put submission at about two working days after the interview. That moved it from 10 November to 23 October, and the provider is TLS Contact, not VFS.
- On Saturday evening you did the unglamorous half.
The France-Visas account, your employer's details for the form, and a request to SBI for an in-principle sanction letter. None of it shows as a tick and all three were holding up the submission.

## What did not
- The SBI branch has not written since 6 October.
Their last substantive word was on 27 September, that verification of the collateral would take more time. Two requests are sitting with them now, not one.
- Your degree originals are still with the courier.
Wednesday's interview needs them in your hand, and nothing on the board says where the parcel is.
- Career did not move at all.
Writing down your post-MBA function, industry and geography is still open, and CareerGlobe, the two questionnaires, the CV and the first CDC session all sit behind it.

## Risks
- The passport window is the one that can cost you the flight.
TLS keeps your passport from submission until the decision, about fifteen days by Fitria's account. Submitting on 16 October gets it back near the end of the month; submitting on the 23rd gets it back around 7 November, the day you leave Jakarta, and you need it for the KITAS exit permit as well. Every day between the interview and the submission comes off that margin.
- Proof of funds has quietly become a visa problem and not only a tuition one.
The loan used to be a 5 November deadline. The visa file now needs evidence of it too, and both requests sit with the same branch that has gone quiet. If the in-principle letter does not come, the submission has nothing to show.
- One parcel gates the whole visa sequence.
The interview, the submission, the decision and the exit permit all run off a courier nobody has a tracking number for.
- The career chain is the cheapest thing to fix and the most expensive to leave.
One question only you can answer unblocks four tasks, and the first CDC coaching session is already dated 15 November.
